keyVerseText: Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.
rootMeaning: The Greek adverb κάτω (kátō) derives from the preposition κατά and is closely related to the comparative form κατώτερος (katṓteros), meaning "lower" or "inferior," especially in a locative sense such as Hades. This etymology highlights a fundamental spatial concept of being down or beneath, not merely in physical terms but also with connotations of position or rank. The root sense enriches the common English glosses like "down" or "beneath" by emphasizing a relative descent or inferior placement, whether literal or metaphorical.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, κάτω appears 11 times and is most frequently translated as "down" (4 times), "beneath" (3 times), and "the bottom" (2 times), with occasional translations like "under" or "and fell down." This range of translations reflects its consistent core meaning of downward motion or position below something else, whether spatially, as in the nether world, or metaphorically, as in suffering or affliction. The word is versatile, used with verbs implying motion downward, rest beneath, or even geographical positioning, indicating its broad but coherent semantic field.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding κάτω in its original sense as denoting a downward or beneath position deepens our grasp of biblical themes related to human condition, sin, and redemption. It often points to the lowly, the hidden, or the suffering state from which God lifts His people. The word’s connection to the nether world reminds believers of the reality of death and judgment, but also of Christ’s victory over the powers beneath. Thus, κάτω encapsulates the Christian hope that what is lowly or beneath can be raised up by divine grace, underscoring the gospel’s power to transform and elevate.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 2:16, the phrase "from two years old and under" uses κάτω to indicate all children aged two and younger, emphasizing the full extent of Herod’s ruthless command. The word underscores the inclusiveness of this tragic decree, extending to the very bottom age limit within Bethlehem and its surrounding areas. This use of κάτω highlights the severity and thoroughness of the evil intent, contrasting with the protective care God would later show through the preservation of the Christ child.
